Organzie the Symposium on AI in Medicine and Food Sciences
item.description:
SANAD Symposium on AI in Medicine & Food Sciences

Over the past two days, we had the pleasure of hosting our SANAD symposium on AI in Medicine and Food Sciences within the framework of the DAAD Ta’ziz project, welcoming a delegation from Tunisia, Lebanon, and Iraq.
Project link: https://albarqouni.github.io/funded/symposium/

The symposium brought together colleagues from Universitätsklinikum Bonn, The University of Bonn, and our partner universities in the MENA region: Lebanese American University, University of Tunis El Manar, and Duhok Polytechnic University. Together, we focused on strengthening academic cooperation, interdisciplinary exchange, and capacity building under the SANAD vision.

We extend our gratitude to Prof. Björn Krüger for his excellent keynote, to all speakers and participants for their contributions, and to our dedicated team for their support.

Special thanks to Dr. Ismail Acir and his team for co-organizing and hosting the Food Sciences Day with great hospitality.

Beyond the academic program, our delegation enjoyed a rich cultural experience — from the Christmas market in Bonn to the Chocolate Museum and the Cologne Cathedral.

We look forward to building on these connections and continuing our collaboration.

item.title: Contributed to the GLOHRA’s fact-finding mission to Brussels
item.description: I recently had the privilege of joining the Steering Committee of the German Alliance for Global Health Research (GLOHRA) in Brussels for a fact-finding mission from 17–20 November 2025. Alongside colleagues from diverse research disciplines, we engaged in constructive dialogue with key European institutions and partners to better understand the EU’s policy and funding landscape for global health research. Over three days of meetings, we gained valuable insights into emerging priorities for research funding and the upcoming EU Framework Programme (FP10), identifying new opportunities for collaboration and coordinated action from the research community. This visit not only strengthened our understanding of how global health research can be supported at the EU level but also reinforced our collective commitment to advancing impactful, interdisciplinary research that addresses global health challenges.

item.title: Organzie the Summer School on Biomedical Imaging with Deep Learning (BiLD)
item.description:
We have just wrapped up an inspiring week of the BILD Summer School 2025 in Tunis, and I could not be more grateful for the people and partnerships that made this possible.

A heartfelt thank you to the University of Tunis El Manar, represented by the Rector Prof. Moez CHAFRA and his vice rectors, for their warm welcome and strong support of this initiative. Your presence was an honor and an encouragement to all of us.

My sincere gratitude also goes to my co-organizers, Prof. Monia Najar, Bareen Haval, and Prof. Hussein F. HASSAN, PhD, for their trust and collaboration!

I would like to thank all the speakers and lecturers, Prof. Nassir Navab, Prof. Vasileios Belagiannis, Prof. Islem Rekik, Prof. Ezzeddine Zagrouba, Prof. Hanene Boussi, and Dr. Narjes Ben ameur, Dr. Aditya Rastogi, Dr. Lara Marie Reimer, Leon Nissen, and Rached Abdelkhalek for their amazing talks and lectures.

A special thanks to the tutors: David D. Gaviria, Diletta Chiaro, Ph.D., Elyes Farjallah, Hadil AFFES, and Sarra Guirat for preparing and tutoring a couple of exercises and hands-on sessions during the summer school.

Thanks to our participants, who made it from Lebanon, Iraq, Germany (Ulm, Essen, Munich, and Bonn), and multiple cities in Tunisia (Tunis, Bizerte, Sousse, Sfax, and Kebili), for their dedication and curiosity!

Each of you contributed your expertise, energy, and enthusiasm, turning this event into a true success story.

Highlights of the week:

  • Engaging lectures that bridged theory and real-world applications in biomedical imaging and AI.
  • Hands-on sessions where students trained, tested, and discussed DL models—exploring both the challenges and opportunities of deep learning in medical imaging.
  • Special Hands-on Sessions on MONAI Labels from NVIDIA (Rached Abdelkhalek) and Mobile Medical AI App Development (Lara Marie Reimer and Leon Nissen)
  • Networking events that fostered meaningful connections and future collaborations across countries and disciplines.

This summer school once again underscored the core mission of the SANAD Project: knowledge exchange and building sustainable networks.

This won’t happen without the support of our medical faculty at the Universitätsklinikum Bonn, represented by the Dean, Prof. Bernd Weber, and the DAAD German Academic Exchange Service, with funds from the Auswärtiges Amt (Federal Foreign Office) Germany in Germany.

We look forward to seeing the seeds planted in Tunis grow into lasting collaborations and innovations!

Interested to learn more about the experience shared by our participants, feel free to visit the testimonials page here: https://lnkd.in/dxVAnG75.

Interested to join us for the upcoming summer/autumn schools, follow our homepage ( https://lnkd.in/dEANjkhs) and LinkedIn Post

item.title: Participated at the AI for Good Global Summit in Geneva, Switzerland
item.description:
Just returned from my first AI for Good Global Summit in Geneva — an incredible experience!

I was especially inspired by the focus on AI in healthcare:

  • Reversing diabetes and Parkinson’s with AI-powered stem cell therapies
  • Real-time, personalized health risk screening using AI
  • Tackling global health inequities with open, responsible, and equitable AI solutions

This summit reminded me that AI is not just about innovation — it’s about impact. Excited to keep learning and contributing to this global movement

item.title: Panelist at Applied Case Studies of AI in Health for WHO EMRO Workshop, Egypt
item.description: Honored to join an inspiring panel at the WHO EMRO AI Workshop on Applied Case Studies of AI in Health, alongside brilliant colleagues working at the intersection of AI, public health, and policy. I shared insights from our work at the University of Bonn on building trustworthy and equitable AI models for medical imaging—especially in global health settings where data diversity and clinical applicability are key challenges. Grateful for the engaging discussion on how we can ensure that AI innovations serve not just high-resource settings, but also strengthen health systems worldwide

item.title: Elodie attended and presented at the 2024 International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP) in Abu Dhabi, UAE
item.description: Elodie had the chance to attend the 2024 IEEE International Conference on Image Processing in Abu Dhabi, Emirates. She presented her work during an oral session about Medical Image Analysis. This work was part of her Ph.D. projects and was entitled Uncovering communities of pipelines in the task fMRI analytical space. In this work, she used graph representations to explore the relationships between fMRI pipelines results and the stability of their relationships across different study contexts. The results were useful to evaluate the potential generalisability and robustness to unseen context of methods to mitigate analytical variability, for instance, style transfer between statistic maps.
